newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia won't issue UES convertible eurobond in Dec.
newsitem.headline: Russia won't issue UES convertible eurobond in Dec.

text.p: Russia's privatisation ministry, the State Property Committee (GKI), does not plan in December to issue a Eurobond convertible into shares in national power company Unified Energy System (UES), a GKI source said on Monday.
Privatisation officials said in September that a Eurobond convertible into 7.50 percent of UES would be sold later this year.

Last week privatisation authorities announced that 3.66 billion shares or 8.5 percent of the capital of UES (RAO Yedinaya Energeticheskaya Sistema Rossii) would be sold at a cash auction with bids accepted from November 22 to December 23.
The GKI source said the issue was being delayed because UES, Russia's biggest company by sales and employees, and one of its most liquid shares, was "insufficiently open".
A source at UES said the advisers to the issue had said it was not technically possible to undertake such a complicated financial transaction by the end of the year.
UES has not yet published financials restated to international accounting standards, but has announced plans to issue American Depositary Receipts.
But the decision to go ahead with the cash auction of the 8.5 percent stake would seem to rule out a convertible Eurobond for UES altogether.
Altogether the government owns 60 percent of UES, but has said it will keep 51 percent until 1998.
The issue would have been Russia's first convertible Eurobond.
Alexander Lopatin, UES director of asset management, told Reuters the company might proceed with a Eurobond of its own, but one which would not be convertible into or collateralised with UES shares.
Two other large companies, gas monopoly RAO Gazprom and Russia's biggest oil group, NK LUKoil, are talking of doing corporate Eurobonds.
Several municipalities, including Moscow and St Petersburg, have also announced Eurobond plans.
But Finance Minister Alexander Livshits said last week the federal authorities would control access for Russian borrowers to the Euromarket.
Russia's debut sovereign Eurobond was heavily oversubscribed last week, despite the volume being increased to $1 billion and maturity extended to five years.
The GKI had named CS First Boston as global coordinator for the UES bond.
At 0930 GMT had fallen to $0.0818 from Friday's closing $0.0825.
